summary: This note surveys the genres of a local music scene: punk, jazz, indie rock, hip hop, folk and roots, and genre-defying eclectic acts. It names artists, venues and events from September to November 2023, and argues that the scene's variety makes it a crossroads of ideas, passions and sounds.
one_line: A genre-by-genre tour of the local music scene, featuring artists, venues and events from fall 2023, celebrating its diversity.
key_facts: Punk rock has been the soundtrack of youthful rebellion and social commentary since its explosion in the mid-1970s, and new local bands carry it on as of October 7, 2023.
The Broken Bottles and Fistful of Conviction are local punk bands named in the note.
Fistful of Conviction frontman James "Riot" Keller said at a show on September 15, 2023: "It's not just music, it's a movement."
The Velvet Note and Blue Cat Café are named as local jazz venues.
Pianist Samantha "Soulfingers" Jones played her latest album at the Blue Cat Café on September 22, 2023, alongside the jazz trio Nuance in the scene.
Indie rock bands Lighthouse Mornings and Echo Park Satellite have a dedicated following for their hooks, lyrical depth and artistic integrity.
Lighthouse Mornings performed at The Marquee on October 13, 2023, and fans sang every word back to the band.
Hip hop artists T-Kay47 and Lyricist Supreme address social issues, personal struggles and triumphs in their rhymes.
T-Kay47 performed at a battle rap event on September 30, 2023, praised for technical prowess and raw authenticity.
The Rambling Souls and solo act Maggie McCall reinterpret traditional folk music.
Maggie McCall played the Harvest Folk Festival on October 20, 2023, reinterpreting folk classics for a captivated crowd.
The Cosmic Experiment gave a concert on November 5, 2023, blending electronica, world beats and avantgarde rock, and Sonic Tapestry is cited as an instrumental act that defies categorization.
The note concludes that the local music scene is a crossroads where different paths meet.
